issues.body: `_features_table()` reads only `data["features"]`, and `check_declared_sensitive_features()` iterates only those keys. Cargo also declares an implicit feature for each optional dependency when that dependency is not referenced via `dep:<name>` in the feature table. For example, `[dependencies] foo = { version = "...", optional = true }` plus `#![cfg(feature = "foo")]` defines a real sensitive Cargo feature, but this check never classifies `foo`. If no leg activates it, `--enforce` still reports success, contradicting invariant (3)'s stated purpose and completeness claim.
issues.fix_hint: Parse dependency tables (including target-specific dependency tables as applicable) and add optional dependency names that Cargo exposes as implicit features, excluding names whose implicit feature is suppressed by a `dep:<name>` reference. Add a hermetic regression test with an optional dependency, a `cfg(feature = "<dependency-name>")` test, and no leg activating it; assert `check_declared_sensitive_features` returns `VIOLATION(3)`.
issues.title: Implicit optional-dependency features are not enumerated

verdict.summary: The new invariant is wired into enforcement and its direct tests pass, but its declared-feature enumeration is incomplete relative to Cargo's feature model. Cargo creates implicit features for optional dependencies unless the dependency is referenced with `dep:` syntax; those features do not appear as keys in `[features]`. Because `_features_table` returns only that table, a sensitive implicit optional-dependency feature with no matrix leg remains invisible, preserving the zero-leg blind spot this PR claims to close.
